transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

I’ve been taking on way more than I normally would. I went from just being one of the crew to trying to run three bids, call city people, line up plant suppliers, and message everybody I know about this park idea. It felt like I just couldn’t shut it off.
Before this started, have you ever experienced a period in your life where you felt deeply down or depressed for weeks at a time?
Yeah. It’s been hanging over me for about a year now. This latest crash is the worst it’s gotten.
Are you feeling deeply down or depressed right now?
Yeah. It’s been hanging over me for about a year, but this latest crash is the worst it’s gotten.
Are you still feeling that revved-up drive and inability to shut off right now, at the same time as this crash?
Yeah, I still feel driven to keep doing things. I was up before daylight loading tools, sketching out beds, pricing native plants—and even after a full day outside, I felt like I had to keep going.

latest_inference.note: Patient confirms concurrent depressive ('crash') and hypomanic/manic ('driven to keep doing things', decreased need for sleep, revved-up) symptoms, meeting criteria for a mixed episode (F31.6) and ruling out pure depressive episodes (F31.3, F31.4, F31.5).

inference_history.note: Initial presentation of increased goal-directed activity, excessive planning, and inability to 'shut it off' suggests a manic or hypomanic state, either unipolar, bipolar, or secondary to another medical/substance etiology.
